rule_findings.label: High Jitter
rule_findings.summary: Elevated cycle-to-cycle pitch perturbation suggests reduced vocal stability and possible physiological arousal.

rule_findings.label: High Pause Ratio
rule_findings.summary: Frequent or extended pauses may reflect hesitation, cognitive load, avoidance, or disrupted speech flow.

rule_findings.label: Low Vocal Energy
rule_findings.summary: Reduced vocal intensity may indicate flattened expression, fatigue, withdrawal, or low activation.

rule_findings.label: High Pitch Variability
rule_findings.summary: Large pitch variation may suggest unstable vocal control during depression-relevant affective states.

rule_findings.label: High Mean Pitch
rule_findings.summary: Raised average pitch can be consistent with affective tension or altered activation, depending on speaker baseline.

rule_findings.label: Low Mean Pitch
rule_findings.summary: Lowered average pitch can appear with reduced expressivity, fatigue, or psychomotor slowing.

rule_findings.label: High MFCC 1 Mean
rule_findings.summary: A shifted first cepstral coefficient may reflect broad spectral-energy changes in the voice.

rule_findings.label: High MFCC 2 Variability
rule_findings.summary: Greater spectral-shape variability can indicate inconsistent articulation or affective instability.

rule_findings.label: Low MFCC 3 Mean
rule_findings.summary: A low third cepstral coefficient may indicate altered spectral balance requiring contextual review.

rule_findings.label: High MFCC 4 Variability
rule_findings.summary: Higher mid-cepstral variability may reflect unstable speech production across the recording.

Explain the retrieved graph paths from biomarkers to clinical concepts, screening constructs, risk, and follow-up. Mention edge-level sources when useful.
If previous-week context is supplied, compare the current aggregate evidence with prior weeks while clearly marking simulated context as synthetic.
Avoid inferred PHQ-8 scores, diagnosis, medication advice, or unsupported high-risk claims.
